bugs.summary: The new --grace-period CLI flag is an unvalidated f64 passed straight to Duration::mul_f64, so a negative, NaN or very large value (e.g. --grace-period -1) panics the client as soon as a quorum is reached.
bugs.evidence: linera-client/src/client_options.rs:162-163 `#[arg(long, default_value_t = DEFAULT_GRACE_PERIOD)] pub grace_period: f64` has no value_parser or range check; linera-client/src/client_context.rs:177 and linera-core/src/client/mod.rs:211,275,1123,1159,1530,1688 pass it through unchanged; linera-core/src/updater.rs:180 `start_time.elapsed().mul_f64(grace_period)`. std::time::Duration::mul_f64 documents: "Panics: This method will panic if result is negative, overflows Duration or not finite." No fix: linera-io/linera-protocol main still exposes the flag (now quorum_grace_period, client_options.rs:206-207) without validation. AACR-Bench Repo Level comment on updater.rs:139 (base-relative).

rejected.was: model cluster: unvalidated --grace-period panics in Duration::mul_f64 (client_options.rs:159-163, updater.rs:140-185, ~30 findings)
model cluster: impossible-quorum case now breaks immediately instead of waiting the grace period (updater.rs:170-185, ~16 findings)
rejected.why: Intended behaviour: the PR description lists 'Refactored the end_time setting logic ... to improve the handling of unreachable quorum', and upstream main keeps the same early `break 'vote_wait` (updater.rs:279-281). Error groups reaching validity_threshold still return Trusted immediately (:161-165).

rejected.was: model finding: temporary client in assign_new_chain_to_key ignores the user's --grace-period (linera-service main.rs:1250)
rejected.why: That client only calls download_certificates and local_node queries (main.rs:1272-1283); grace_period is read only by ChainClient quorum calls, so the value has no effect there.
